title: Audit logging: emit structured events for Dedicated rollout actions
author: Kevin Osei
body: Context: Dedicated staged rollouts add manual approvals/aborts and evaluator-driven holds; enterprise customers have asked for a compliance-grade audit trail (SUP-3981) that ties each action to an actor and scoped Dedicated resources. This PR emits structured audit events for rollout plan and stage lifecycle actions from the control-plane API (create/update/approve/abort/auto-hold), including actor, tenant, pool_id, plan_id, plan_version, and stage_id where applicable, and routes events through the existing audit export pipeline. Changes: (1) Define rollout-specific audit event types and a stable payload contract (no free-form JSON) with explicit allowlisted fields; (2) Emit audit events at the API boundary after authorization + persistence succeed (so events represent committed state); (3) Normalize actor extraction from auth context (user vs service token) and include request_id for correlation; (4) Add unit tests for emission and schema validation and an integration-style test for event fanout to the audit publisher interface; (5) Add minimal docs/comments for operators on how to filter in SIEM by tenant_id/pool_id/plan_id. Event types (new): rollout.plan.created, rollout.plan.updated, rollout.stage.approved, rollout.stage.aborted, rollout.stage.auto_hold, rollout.stage.advanced (emitted when stage state transitions due to evaluator/approval). Notes: stage_id is populated for stage-scoped actions; for plan-scoped actions stage_id is omitted; plan_version is always populated from the persisted plan record (optimistic concurrency version). PII: no prompts, request bodies, or model outputs are logged; actor display_name/email are not included (only actor_id + actor_type).
commits: audit: add rollout audit event definitions + payload allowlist
control-plane: emit audit events for rollout CRUD + stage actions
auth: normalize actor identity extraction for audit logging
tests: verify rollout audit emission and schema validation
docs: add SIEM filtering examples in audit logging notes
conversation: Marcus Lin (Security): Payload looks good but please ensure we never log user email/display name. Also want explicit documentation of which fields are emitted so reviewers can confirm no sensitive data slips in later. Kevin Osei (Author): Ack; actor will be (actor_type, actor_id) only. Added an allowlist struct + tests that fail if new fields are added without updating the contract, and added internal docs with the exact schema. Kaitlyn Nguyen (RBAC): Where are events emitted relative to authz and persistence? We should not emit on rejected requests, and we should not emit before commit because retries could create phantom entries. Kevin Osei: Emission happens after permission check and after the DB write returns success; for approve/abort we emit after the stage transition transaction commits; tests cover no-emission on 403 and on persistence error. Ethan Park (Control plane): plan_version needs to come from the stored plan row, not from request payload; also watch out for concurrent approvals where optimistic concurrency increments the version. Kevin Osei: Updated to source plan_version from the post-write plan record; for stage transitions we re-read the plan version inside the same transaction and include it in the event. Added a regression test that simulates version bump. Felix Schneider (Console backend): For UI audit view we’ll likely page by plan_id and stage_id; can we guarantee stage_id is present on approve/abort/auto-hold? Kevin Osei: Yes; stage_id is required for stage actions and validated at handler boundary; plan-level events omit it. Sean Gallagher (SRE): Can we include request_id and pool_id to correlate with incidents? Also, please keep cardinality under control (avoid adding per-request extra fields like route/model names here). Kevin Osei: Included request_id and pool_id; explicitly not including route/model. CI green; Marcus approved after doc/test additions. Merged via squash.
release_notes: Added structured audit log events for Dedicated staged rollout actions (plan create/update, stage approve/abort/auto-hold/advance) including actor, tenant_id, pool_id, plan_id, plan_version, and stage_id (where applicable).
